memory_update.text: AMSC is the highest-priority US-listed underfollowed candidate for this node because D-VAR is directly mapped to STATCOM/reactive-power/grid-stability use cases.

PLPC should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a second-order transmission-hardware candidate, but survival depends on evidence of high-voltage project exposure, utility qualification stickiness, or HVDC/substation linkage.
POWL is a speculative-shadow candidate for FACTS/HVDC balance-of-plant and utility/industrial electrical-control infrastructure; direct node evidence is currently weak.
GE Vernova is the reference anchor for HVDC/FACTS/STATCOM/reactor/capacitor mapping and should be used to identify subsystem suppliers rather than as the main underfollowed alpha target.

The strongest pure-play evidence for reactors, harmonic filters, instrument transformers, STATCOM-adjacent components, and HVDC/FACTS customer wins appears to include non-US-listed companies such as India's Quality Power Electrical Equipments; US-listed equivalents may be scarce or hidden in broader industrials.

node: HVDC, FACTS, reactors, harmonic filters, instrument transformers, and grid-stability components
summary: Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe for HVDC/FACTS and grid-stability hardware. The cleanest direct US-listed small/mid-cap exposure found is AMSC through D-VAR STATCOM/reactive-power systems. GE Vernova is the obvious reference leader for HVDC, FACTS, STATCOM, reactors, and capacitors but is mega-cap/high-attention. PLPC is an underfollowed transmission-hardware supplier with plausible second-order exposure to high-voltage grid buildout, though not yet proven as a direct HVDC/FACTS reactor/filter supplier. POWL is a larger-cap second-order candidate supplying custom electrical distribution/control equipment to utilities and industrials; its direct relation to HVDC/FACTS stations requires verification. Non-US-listed evidence, especially Quality Power Electrical Equipments in India, reinforces that the actual scarce-supplier pool may sit outside US exchanges, creating a US-listed coverage gap.
